1.judul: Case Study 1 — Documentary Discrepancies (Invoice vs. Goods Received)
1.deskripsi:
A vendor sends an invoice for 100 laptop units.
• However, when you check the Travel Document/Proof of Goods Receipt from the warehouse, it turns out that the warehouse only received 90 laptop units (10 units were defective and returned).
• Vendors insist on being paid for the full 100 units according to the invoice they printed.

pertanyaan.1: Why are AP staff strictly prohibited from processing payments just by looking at an invoice from the vendor without checking the receipt documents from the warehouse?
pertanyaan.2: What actions should you take to mediate data differences between your company's Vendor and Warehouse parties?
pertanyaan.3: Write a 1 sentence tactical reply to the vendor explaining why you will only transfer money for 90 units, without offending them.

2.judul: Case Study 2 — Vendor Threat & Cash Flow Crisis
2.deskripsi:
The raw material vendor was furious because his bill had been paid 2 weeks late.They threatened to stop delivery of goods tomorrow morning.
• Your Financial Manager instructed you to withhold all payments because the company's cash is empty and new money will come in next week.

pertanyaan.1: If you are afraid of being scolded and then ignore calls from vendors (ghosting), what is the worst impact on your company's factory operations tomorrow morning?
pertanyaan.2: You are caught between the boss's instructions (empty cash) and the vendor's threats.How do you act professionally on the phone when faced with the vendor's anger?
pertanyaan.3: Write 1 negotiation sentence to calm the vendor, convincing them that the money will definitely be paid next week so that tomorrow's delivery of goods will not be stopped.

3.judul: Case Study 3 — The Dangers of Double Billing
3.deskripsi:
You receive an AC service bill invoice worth IDR 10,000,000.When you are about to enter it into the system, you feel familiar and find that the bill with the PO (Purchase Order) number and the exact same amount was paid last month.
• The vendor argues it's just a "misprint from their system" and insists you pay it anyway.

pertanyaan.1: What are the fatal losses for the company and your career if you are careless in making double transfers (double payments) for the same job?
pertanyaan.2: Mention 2 pieces of evidence of documents/data that you must capture or show to the vendor to prove that the bill was paid in full last month.
pertanyaan.3: Create 1 simple SOP (Checking Rule) at the AP's work desk so that cases of missed double payments never occur.

4.judul: Case Study 4 — Tax Cut (PPh) Protest
4.deskripsi:
A freelance consultant sent a service bill of IDR 10,000,000.
• As an AP, the rules require you to deduct Income Tax (PPh 21), so that the money transferred to the account is less than 10 million.
• The consultant protested loudly: "I don't want to know about taxes, basically 10 million has to go into my account!"

pertanyaan.1: Why is the company (through AP staff) obliged to deduct the tax directly, instead of letting the consultant take care of the tax himself?
pertanyaan.2: Write 1 sentence of simple explanation (layman's language) to the consultant so that he understands that the deduction is an absolute rule from the State, not because the company is stingy!
pertanyaan.3: If a boss from another division tells you: "That's it, just pay the full 10 million, we'll just hide the tax so he doesn't get angry."What is your emphatic response as an AP person?

5.judul: Case Study 5 — Unsigned Emergency Payments
5.deskripsi:
The director is abroad and cannot be contacted.Suddenly, the Marketing Manager comes to the AP's desk and urges you to immediately transfer the DP (Down Payment) for the building rental of IDR 50,000,000 for the event tomorrow morning.
• There is no official document (PO) or signature of the Director's approval.
• The manager said: "Just transfer now, if there is a problem, I will put the responsibility on it!"

pertanyaan.1: In terms of financial audit, why can't the Marketing Manager's "I'm the one doing it" excuse protect you if problems occur in the future?
pertanyaan.2: What is the worst risk if AP gets into the habit of transferring tens of millions using only words or verbal orders without written documents?
pertanyaan.3: You are prohibited from transferring without approval, but tomorrow's event must still go ahead.Propose 1 way out/alternative solution so that the Marketing Manager can still legally pay the down payment for the building today.

1.judul: Case Study 1 — Dealing with Client Ghosting (Running Away from the Bill)
1.deskripsi:
A large client has not paid a bill that is 30 days past due.
• When you don't pick up your phone and don't reply to your email (ghosting).
• The Sales team at the office tells you: "Just wait, don't charge too hard, he's an important client, then he'll get angry and run away to a competitor."

pertanyaan.1: Why does obeying the words of the Sales team to "just wait" endanger our company's cash flow?
pertanyaan.2: Since this client likes ghosting, what 1 firm but professional action would you take besides constantly calling/WhatsApping?
pertanyaan.3: Write a draft of a short message to the client urging payment, without sounding like a threat from a debt collector.

2.judul: Case Study 2 — Credit Limit Conflict (AR vs Sales Team)
2.deskripsi:
A client has reached the maximum debt limit (Credit Limit) and is still in arrears on last month's payment.
• Suddenly, the Sales Manager forces you to unblock the system today so that the client's new order can be sent.
• The Sales Manager promises: "Just open the system, I guarantee you the old bill will be transferred tomorrow!"

pertanyaan.1: In terms of financial audit, why should the Sales Manager's verbal guarantee "will definitely be paid tomorrow" not be used as a basis for unblocking the system?
pertanyaan.2: If you are determined to obey the Sales Manager and the client turns out to be in default/bankrupt, who will the auditor/company blame most: you (AR) or the Sales Manager?Explain why.
pertanyaan.3: Write 1 sentence in a firm reply to the Sales Manager to reject his request, but provide 1 solution condition if the item must be sent today.

3.judul: Case Study 3 — Partial Payment Deductions
3.deskripsi:
The client transferred the bill, but the amount was less than 20% of the total invoice.
• When confirmed, the client reasoned: "Yesterday there was a slightly defective item, so I just cut the payment myself by 20% as compensation."
• In fact, the client has never reported to your office about the defective item before.

pertanyaan.1: Why does the client's action of unilaterally deducting payments violate the receivables administration (AR) rules?
pertanyaan.2: Which internal department should you contact first to validate the truth of what the client said about the defective item?
pertanyaan.3: Write 1 sentence explaining to the client that they still have to pay the remaining 20% ​​today, and explain the correct procedure if there is a return/defective item.

4.judul: Case Study 4 — The Mystery of Unidentified Transfers
4.deskripsi:
There is money coming into the company account amounting to IDR 25,000,000.
• However, in the bank statement there is no sender's name, no transfer information, and no Invoice number.
• At the same time, there are 3 different clients whose nominal debts are similar in that figure.

pertanyaan.1: What's the danger if you just guess and immediately enter the payment to reduce client A's debt (the client who has been in the longest in arrears)?
pertanyaan.2: Instead of asking all clients one by one, mention 2 ways/supporting data that you can check to confirm who the original sender of the money is!
pertanyaan.3: Create 1 simple rule/SOP that must be conveyed by the Sales team to all clients so that this "anonymous transfer" problem does not happen again.

5.judul: Case Study 5 — Fake Transfer Evidence (Fast Fraud Mode)
5.deskripsi:
A new client sent a photo/screenshot of proof of m-Banking transfer via WhatsApp in the afternoon.
• He urges you to immediately issue a Travel Document so that the goods can be picked up by the courier right away.
• However, when you check the company's Internet Banking statement, the money hasn't arrived at all.
• The client reasons: "It's a different bank, it's normal for it to take a long time to arrive. Just send the goods first, I've already sent proof of the transfer!"

pertanyaan.1: As an AR, why will screenshots of proof of transfer from clients never be considered as valid proof of payment?
pertanyaan.2: Faced with the demands of an angry client asking for goods to be sent quickly, what is your absolute decision that afternoon: Send the goods OR Hold the goods?
pertanyaan.3: Write a standard 1-sentence reply to the client explaining the company's goods release rules, without directly accusing the client of the transfer receipt being fake.

1.judul: Case Study 1 — Errors in Recording Past Profits
1.deskripsi:
In PT Alpha's 2026 bookkeeping report, there is an addition of "Initial Retained Profit" of IDR 800,000,000.
• This addition arose because the accounting department just realized there was an error in calculating the depreciation costs for assets (such as machines/buildings) in the previous two years (2024 and 2025).
• As a result of improvements that increase profits, the company must also calculate the effect of a tax deduction of IDR 176,000,000.

pertanyaan.1: Because these improvements (corrections) from the past result in an increase in the current earnings balance, what kind of calculation errors did the accounting team actually make in the 2024 and 2025 asset cost reports?
pertanyaan.2: Why can't the repair figure of IDR 800,000,000 not just be recorded as "Other Income" in the 2026 profit and loss report, but must be included directly in Retained Earnings?
pertanyaan.3: When you prepare your company's wealth report (Balance Sheet) at the end of 2026, you are also required to display a comparison table with the 2025 figures. What adjustments should you make to the asset value records and tax payable records in the 2025 column so that the report makes sense?

2.judul: Case Study 2 — Internal Transactions of Parent and Subsidiaries
2.deskripsi:
At the end of the year, when preparing combined (consolidated) financial statements between the Parent and Subsidiaries, accountants must "clear" the records of buying and selling transactions between themselves.
• The write-off (elimination) journal made is: Deleting Sales Revenue of Rp. 1,000,000,000 (Debit), reducing the Cost of Goods Sold/COGS of Rp. 800,000,000 (Credit), and deducting the Inventory value of Rp. 200,000,000 (Credit).

pertanyaan.1: What is the initial capital and selling price between these companies?Then, why does the inventory value have to be cut by IDR 200,000,000 at the end of the year?
pertanyaan.2: If the Subsidiary sells to the Parent, why does this deduction of IDR 200,000,000 reduce the profit share for minority shareholders?
pertanyaan.3: If the remaining goods are finally sold to outside parties next year, how do you recognize this delayed profit in next year's report?

4.deskripsi:

3.judul: Case Study 3 — FIFO System Failure and Messy Rack Layout
3.deskripsi:
Your warehouse must use a FIFO (First In, First Out) system, meaning that the goods that are first in must be the first to go out.The computer has told the officer to take the Old Batch goods (expiry next month).
• However, the field staff instead took the New Batch (expiry next year).
• The reason is that the Old Batch goods are stuck on the back shelf and are blocked by a pile of New Batch goods that just arrived yesterday.
• Officers are lazy to dismantle the pile, so the Old Batch goods end up rotting/expired in the warehouse.

pertanyaan.1: What fatal mistake did the officer make when placing newly arrived goods, so that the old batch of goods became obstructed and difficult for the packing team to pick up?
pertanyaan.2: In terms of work safety and convenience, which position is better for placing heavy and large New Batch items: on the bottom floor at the front of the shelf, or at the top of the back?Give your logical reasons so that workers are not lazy to unload goods.
pertanyaan.3: To dispose of and destroy goods that have already expired from the warehouse computer system, what official documents must be prepared by the warehouse team and must be signed by the Warehouse Manager together with the Finance Manager before the goods are transported out of the factory?

4.judul: Case Study 4 — Broken Goods During Loading and Sudden Changes to the Waybill
4.deskripsi:
You are loading 100 units of hanging lights into a truck for VIP customers.
• When the goods were lifted, 2 lamp units accidentally fell and broke, while the stock in the warehouse had completely run out.
• The truck must leave immediately because time is running out, so it can only carry 98 complete lamps.

pertanyaan.1: The physical goods are only 98 units, but the Road Document (SJ) says 100 units.What emergency measures should you take on the SJ paper so that the factory is not accused of cheating?
pertanyaan.2: If the price of 1 lamp is IDR 1,000,000 and the factory is fined 5% of the total order (100 units) due to insufficient delivery, calculate the value of the fine!How can I explain this accident to the customer so that the fine can be waived?
pertanyaan.3: In the warehouse computer system, the 2 broken lamps were still recorded as goods ready to be shipped.What is the flow or steps on the computer to cancel the delivery of the 2 units and change the status to damaged goods?

5.judul: Case Study 5 — Return of Goods (Reverse Logistics) & Unofficial Documents
5.deskripsi:
A courier truck arrived at the warehouse to return 50 boxes of damaged goods from customers.
• The courier driver only handed you a piece of handwritten paper that said "Goods Damaged, Request Replacement" without an official return document number (RMA) and without any info on your warehouse computer.

pertanyaan.1: The driver forces you to sign a receipt.What are the legal and financial dangers if you just sign before the goods are checked and without an official return number in the system?
pertanyaan.2: If it turns out that the contents of the box were exchanged by customers for fake products to make a profit, how do you secure this evidence so that it doesn't get mixed up with good stock, and which division (Sales or Legal) should be contacted?
pertanyaan.3: If the return turns out to be valid (factory defect), what is the flow in the system to process the two options: (A) Return the customer's money (Refund), or (B) Send new goods without doubling operational costs?

1.judul: Case Study 1 — Falsifying Invoices for End of Year Targets
1.deskripsi:
Towards the end of the year (29 December), the Sales Manager forces you to issue an Invoice and Tax Invoice worth IDR 450,000,000 to Customer A so that the sales division's annual sales target is achieved.
• However, physically, the goods were not ready and were only sent by the warehouse along with the Travel Document (DO) on January 3 of the following year.

pertanyaan.1: If the invoice is still recorded as a sale in December even though the goods have not been shipped, what bad impact will this have on the correctness of the company's financial statements and tax reporting at the end of the year?
pertanyaan.2: The customer finally refused to pay because he felt he had not received the goods.If the financial examiner (auditor) discovers this target manipulation practice, what is the biggest loss for the company?
pertanyaan.3: Since the billing data for December is already "locked" in the computer system and cannot simply be deleted, what correction documents must you make to officially cancel the bill?

2.judul: Case Study 2 — Partial Delivery and Billing Errors
2.deskripsi:
The customer issues a Purchase Order (PO) for 1,000 units of goods.In the system, you create a Sales Order (SO) of 1,000 units.Due to low stock, the warehouse only sent 920 units (Delivery Order / DO).
• However, when processing the invoice, you directly pull the data from the SO and issue an Invoice for 1,000 units.The customer was angry and withheld all payment.

pertanyaan.1: Why is printing invoices based on the initial order quantity (rather than the number of items actually shipped) a fatal mistake?What documents should be matched before a bill is printed?
pertanyaan.2: Because the customer withholds all payments due to this document error, what negative impacts/financial losses will be felt directly by the company?
pertanyaan.3: If the customer previously received a discount for purchasing 1,000 units, what corrective documents should you create now so that the customer is willing to pay for the 920 units, but does not lose his discount rights for the remaining 80 units later?

3.judul: Case Study 3 — Returned Goods and Credit Limit Issues
3.deskripsi:
The customer returned defective goods worth IDR 75,000,000.
• The goods were received by the warehouse at the end of the month, but you postponed recording the return documents in the computer system until next month.
• As a result, when a customer wants to order new goods at the beginning of the month, the system rejects the order automatically because the customer is deemed to have "Full Debt/Credit Limit" (has not paid IDR 75,000,000).

pertanyaan.1: Why can delaying recording returned goods documents in the computer system have fatal consequences and directly harm the company's sales targets for the following month?
pertanyaan.2: According to the correct workflow, name 3 process sequences that should be completed immediately from the moment the physical goods from the customer arrive back at our warehouse door.
pertanyaan.3: Because the customer is angry that his order was rejected and your return documents need time to be processed, what emergency action can you communicate to your superior (Financial Manager) so that the customer's new order can still be processed today?

4.judul: Case Study 4 — Bills Stuck Due to Administrative Errors
4.deskripsi:
An invoice worth IDR 620,000,000 is 45 days past due.
• When billed by the Finance department, the customer refused to pay with the reason: "We have never received the physical bill, and the order number (PO) written on the bill is wrong."
• After investigating, the Sales Admin typed the wrong number because he only received orders via WhatsApp without checking the official email.
• What's worse, the proof of receipt of goods (the delivery letter signed by the customer) was lost by the delivery courier.

pertanyaan.1: Why does losing a receipt and mistyping an order number put a customer in such a strong position to refuse to pay?What are the consequences if the company is determined to take the customer to legal action?
pertanyaan.2: As a Sales Admin, state what supporting documents must be attached with the main bill (Invoice), so that customers cannot look for reasons to reject the bill.
pertanyaan.3: Even though the task of collecting money falls on Finance, what simple precautions should the Sales Admin take a few days after the goods are sent, so that the excuse "the bill has not arrived" never occurs?

5.judul: Case Study 5 — Sales and Warehouse Data Differences
5.deskripsi:
In the end of month report, records in the Sales system show that 2,000 units of goods were sold and billed.
• However, records in the warehouse system show that only 1,850 units of goods actually left the warehouse doors.There is a mysterious difference of 150 units between sales data and physical warehouse data.

pertanyaan.1: Apart from the possibility of the goods being physically lost, how can a Marketing promo program (for example the "Buy 10 Get 1 Free" promo) cause this number difference if the Sales Admin enters the promo code incorrectly in the computer system?
pertanyaan.2: If it turns out that the 150 units were "sold" goods to another shop, why is printing the full bill of sale (Invoice) at this time a big mistake for the company's finances?When should the entrusted goods be recognized as sales?
pertanyaan.3: What document checking steps (data matching) will you take with the Warehouse team to prove exactly where the 150 unit error lies?

1.judul: Case Study 1 — Typo Disaster in Test Result Data
1.deskripsi: QC Analyst in the field submits report paper.On the paper it is written that the Pressure Drop (suction power) figure for the filter is 350 (Normal).However, because you were in a hurry, you typed it into the computer system to 530 (Reject/Defect).As a result, the system automatically locks the item.The Warehouse Team was angry because the goods had to be sent this afternoon but were delayed by the system.

pertanyaan.1: Why are you strictly prohibited from directly editing/changing the number 530 back to 350 in the system secretly without reporting to your superior or field QC?
pertanyaan.2: What impact will operational chaos have on the Warehouse and Sales team if goods that are actually "Good" are instead locked in "Reject" status in the system due to your typo?
pertanyaan.3: Design 1 simple mandatory rule (Double Check SOP) on your desk before you press the Save/Submit button on the computer, so that this number typing error doesn't happen again.

2.judul: Case Study 2 — Coercion to Falsify Documents (CoA)
2.deskripsi: The expedition truck is already on and ready to go to the client's cigarette factory.The Warehouse Team asks you to immediately print the Quality Certificate (CoA).The problem is, the Batch number (Production Code) on the waybill is Batch A, while the lab test results data you hold is for Batch B. The warehouse person urges: "That's it, just edit the Batch number on the CoA paper to become Batch A so the truck can run, the quality will be equally good!"

pertanyaan.1: What is the biggest legal and business risk to the company's good name if you comply with the request to falsify the Batch number on the official CoA document?
pertanyaan.2: When pressured by other operational lines (Warehouse/Logistics) to change data illegally for smooth delivery, what is the official escalation procedure that you must carry out to the Management/QC Supervisor?What limitation parameters determine that you must absolutely refuse to print the CoA before there is written approval (Concession/Deviation Form)?
pertanyaan.3: While holding back the CoA print, what data tracking steps do you immediately carry out on the computer to find out where the original data from Batch A has disappeared?

3.judul: Case Study 3 — Physical vs System Hold State Missed
3.deskripsi: At 10 am, field QC found filters whose glue was damaged and physically attached Red Stickers (HOLD) to the boxes.However, the paper reports pile up on your desk and you forget to click the Hold button on the computer system.As a result, the system still reads that the item has Release status (Good).Warehouse people who did not see the red sticker immediately loaded the goods onto the truck.

pertanyaan.1: According to the Factory SOP, whose mistake was more fatal: the QC Admin who forgot to lock the system OR the Warehouse Person who didn't physically check the cardboard (there was a red sticker)?Give your reasons.
pertanyaan.2: When you realize that there is a gap between the physical status and the system that causes the defective product to be loaded onto the truck, what quick administrative steps should you take in the ERP/WMS system to track the truck coordinates and digitally block the receipt documents on the client's side before the truck arrives at the destination location?
pertanyaan.3: Create a fast communication flow between Field QC and QC Admin so that every time there is a physical Hold status, the item can be immediately locked in the system in less than 5 minutes.

4.judul: Case Study 4 — Loss of "Evidence" (Retain Sample)
4.deskripsi: The client (X Cigarette Factory) called and complained that the filter they received from production 3 months ago was very hard.The QC Manager tells you to look for a "Retain Sample" from that production date on the storage shelf for double checking.Unfortunately, the sample shelf is very messy and the samples from 3 months ago were lost or you forgot to put them away.

pertanyaan.1: Why is the physical loss of the Retain Sample so detrimental to our factory's position when debating a compensation claim with the client?
pertanyaan.2: Because the physical sample is missing, what archive documents (paper/digital) from 3 months ago can you pull out and show to the Manager as replacement evidence that at that time the test results were normal?
pertanyaan.3: Design a labeling and storage system so that monthly Retain Samples are always neat and can be found in less than 3 minutes.

5.judul: Case Study 5 — Missing Calibration & External Audit Schedules
5.deskripsi: Tomorrow morning there will be an External Auditor (client's supervisor) coming to the factory.When you were tidying up your documents (SOP and Calibration) tonight, you just realized that the validity period of the Calibration Certificate for the main measuring instrument in the lab was "Dead/Expired" 2 weeks ago.You forgot to remind the Manager.

pertanyaan.1: If the Auditor knows that the measuring instrument has been out of calibration for 2 weeks, what impact will the quality status of all cigarette filters produced and shipped during those 2 weeks have in the eyes of the law?
pertanyaan.2: Why is negligence in the calibration schedule for this measuring instrument considered a major (very serious) finding that could invalidate the company's ISO certification?
pertanyaan.3: Design a digital calendar system (alert/notification) on the QC Admin computer that can provide automatic warnings to the Quality Manager 30 days, 15 days, and 7 days before the tool calibration expires.

1.judul: Case Study 1 — Import Supplier Low Price Trap
1.deskripsi:
You are tasked with selecting a supplier for packaging materials.The monthly requirement is 10,000 units.You get two offers with the following details:
ParametersVendor A (Local)Vendor B (Imported - China)
Unit PriceIDR 15,000 / unitIDR 11,000 / unit
IncotermsReceive the Arrangement at Our WarehousePick Up Yourself at China Port
Delivery Time5 Days45 Days
Minimum Order10,000 units50,000 units

pertanyaan.1: Vendor B looks IDR 4,000 cheaper.However, because the goods must be picked up by yourself at a foreign port, mention 3 additional hidden costs that we must bear until the goods arrive at the warehouse.
pertanyaan.2: If we choose Vendor B, we are required to buy stock for 5 months at once.What are the bad effects on the factory's cash flow (Cash Flow) and the risk of storage in the warehouse?
pertanyaan.3: Seeing the conditions of shipping costs and the fluctuating dollar exchange rate, give strong reasons why choosing Vendor A (Local) is actually safer for the factory.

2.judul: Case Study 2 — Arranging How to Store Goods (Central vs Regional)
2.deskripsi:
You manage inventory of 4 product categories in electronics retail.Request and cost data are as follows:
SKU CodeMonthly Demand Value (units)Demand Coefficient of Variation (CV)Contribution Margin per UnitShelf Cost per Unit/Month
SKU-A5,000 units0.2 (Very Stable)Rp 50,000Rp 2,000
SKU-B500 units0.9 (Up-Down)Rp 200,000Rp 5,000
SKU-C10,000 units0.3 (Quite Stable)Rp 10,000Rp 500
SKU-D200 units1.5 (Rarely Sold/Seasonal)Rp 50,000Rp 10,000

Strategic Target: Cut total inventory value by 30% but still maintain OTIF (On Time In Full) above 95%.

pertanyaan.1: Which goods should be stored in regional warehouses (near consumers), and which goods should only be stored in the central warehouse to save costs?
pertanyaan.2: If we want to send plain goods from the center and then package/brand them at a regional warehouse, which SKU is most suitable?Mention 2 requirements for a warehouse computer system so that this method is not chaotic.
pertanyaan.3: Because stock has been cut by 30%, mention 3 indicators (KPI) that the SCM Admin must monitor every week so that the store does not run out of goods and consumers are not disappointed.

3.judul: Case Study 3 — The Effect of Swollen Orders on the Supply Chain
3.deskripsi:
Report on the movement of orders for Product Z due to weekend promotions at the retail store (end customer) level.
Supply Chain PointsSales Reality / Actual DemandNumber of Requests (Orders) Forwarded to Upper Parties
Shop Cashier Data (POS)Sold 150 units (up 50 units from usual)Shop ordered 200 units to Distributor
Regional DistributorReceived an order of 200 units from the StoreDistributor ordered 400 units to the Factory
Factory SCM AdminReceived order for 400 units from DistributorSCM order for production of 800 units to Manufacturing

pertanyaan.1: Why did the original sales increase of only 50 units at the store cashier balloon to a production order of 800 units at the factory?Explain the cause of this operational panic.
pertanyaan.2: When the promo period ends and consumer purchases return to normal, what heavy burden or loss will be experienced by the distributor warehouse and factory warehouse as a result of having already produced those 800 units?
pertanyaan.3: As an SCM Admin, what should you do so that the factory computer can directly see the original sales data at the store cashier directly, so that the factory is no longer "lied to" by inflated distributor orders?

4.judul: Case Study 4 — Delivery Truck Jam and Full Warehouse
4.deskripsi: Approaching Eid, goods shipments jumped 300%.The company uses external expedition services (truck vendors/3PL).Unfortunately, their trucks often arrive late at the warehouse.As a result, goods pile up and clog the warehouse loading dock area.

pertanyaan.1: The warehouse door was crowded because the truck was late.What are the bad consequences for workers in the warehouse who want to pick up goods or arrange goods on shelves?
pertanyaan.2: How to implement a Cross-Docking system (new goods from the factory are transferred directly to courier trucks without being stored on shelves) to break down this bottleneck?
pertanyaan.3: Relying on a single expedition vendor can prove risky.As SCM Admin, what are your plans for managing truck vendors for next year's peak season so that this problem doesn't happen again?

5.judul: Case Study 5 — Withdrawal of Damaged Goods from the Market (Reverse Logistics)
5.deskripsi: BPOM ordered a product recall for one snack production code number (batch) because it was contaminated.As an SCM Admin, you must withdraw 10,000 boxes of products that have already been distributed to 50 agents throughout Indonesia to be returned to the central warehouse.

pertanyaan.1: What is the first step you must enter into the computer so that the product with the contaminated code number (batch) is automatically locked and cannot be sold to consumers again?
pertanyaan.2: When return trucks arrive at the central warehouse, how do you set up the quarantine area so that damaged goods don't accidentally get mixed up with good goods ready to be sold?
pertanyaan.3: Withdrawing this item does not make money, instead it costs a lot of money.Mention the 3 main logistics cost components that the company must pay as a result of this national scale goods withdrawal process.

1.judul: Case Study 1 — ATK & Pantry Stock Control (Daily Inventory)
1.deskripsi: Every month, the Office Stationery (ATK) and Pantry budget is always over-budgeted and stock runs out in the middle of the month.During this time, items were placed in open cupboards and were free for anyone to take.GA managers task you with stopping this waste and turning it into a financially trackable system.

pertanyaan.1: Create a short flow (maximum 3 stages) regarding the new way for employees to request stationery from GA, so that outgoing goods are recorded neatly but don't make employees feel complicated.
pertanyaan.2: What is the most logical and simple way to determine the "Minimum Stock Limit" on the shelf, so that you know when is the right time to order goods from a vendor before the stock is completely empty?
pertanyaan.3: Many employees protested and considered GA to be "stingy" now.Write 1 sentence in a polite and tactical reply to explain that this new rule is purely about system neatness, not because it is stingy.

2.judul: Case Study 2 — Scheduling Dilemma (AC Washing vs VVIP Meeting)
2.deskripsi: The routine AC cleaning schedule for the meeting room falls today at 09.00.The problem is, this afternoon at 13.00 there was an impromptu meeting of the VVIP Director and Client in that room.Suddenly, the vendor technician informed them that they were 1.5 hours late (only arrived at 10.30).

pertanyaan.1: Faced with a vendor who is 1.5 hours late, what is your quick decision: Cancel washing the AC today OR Force them to keep washing the AC?Give your operational reasons considering the VVIP meeting at 13.00.
pertanyaan.2: Apart from asking for before and after photos of the job, what specific technical data/evidence should you ask for to avoid being lied to by vendors?
pertanyaan.3: Create 1 "Cleanliness SLA" clause that binds vendors.What specific punishment (penalty) will you give if after washing the AC, they leave the meeting room carpet wet and dirty?

3.judul: Case Study 3 — Vendor Management & Legal Compliance (Outsourcing)
3.deskripsi: Employees complain that toilets are dirty and parking is unsafe.Cleaning Service and Security vendor services have decreased drastically.They still have 8 months left on their contract, and there is a 30% penalty for the company if GA terminates the contract unilaterally.

pertanyaan.1: To ensure that employee complaints are valid and not subjective opinions, design 2 objective parameters for carrying out Incidental Audits (sudden inspections) of toilets and parking areas.
pertanyaan.2: You plan to terminate the vendor's contract next month without having to pay the 30% penalty.What 2 operational/legal documents do you absolutely have to collect starting today as "weapons/evidence" of their negligence?
pertanyaan.3: Propose a simple reporting system that involves daily employee participation, so that GA can monitor toilet cleanliness without having to patrol the field every hour.

4.judul: Case Study 4 — IT Asset Maintenance (Printer Malfunction Investigation)
4.deskripsi: The large printer machine on the 2nd floor often breaks down (paper gets stuck), even though it was only serviced last week.You suspect that this is not the vendor's fault, but rather that employees on the 2nd floor often forcefully pull jammed paper and use waste paper that still has staples in it.

pertanyaan.1: How do you tactically investigate and look for evidence for your suspicions, without appearing to directly accuse the people on the 2nd floor?
pertanyaan.2: If the machine has to be taken to the vendor's workshop for 3 days, arrange a printing transfer protocol to the 1st floor machine so that confidential documents (such as HRD salary slips or finance bills) are not leaked and read by other employees.
pertanyaan.3: Design 1 visual warning message (a small poster near the machine) to discourage the habit of stapling paper, without using harsh/lecturing no-words.

5.judul: Case Study 5 — Execution Supervision (BAST) & K3 Assertiveness (HSE)
5.deskripsi: The building vendor reported via WhatsApp that the repair of the leaking door hinges and pantry pipe was 100% complete.They urge you to immediately sign the Minutes of Handover (BAST) so that their workers' wages can be disbursed this afternoon.

pertanyaan.1: What are the financial and professional risks for your own career if you immediately sign the BAST using only a photo report from the vendor, without carrying out a physical check in the field?
pertanyaan.2: When physically checked, it turned out that the pantry pipe was still dripping slightly.Design a BAST rejection sentence that is diplomatic, but firmly forces the vendor to work overtime to complete it on the same day.
pertanyaan.3: While working, the vendor technician insisted on not wanting to wear K3 equipment (such as safety belts/protective glasses) because he felt it was "complicated".Arrange 1 instant action in that second to force them to comply without having to make a fuss in the office.

1.judul: Case Study 1 — Fatal Mistake (Salary Overpayment)
1.deskripsi: You made a typo when processing your salary.As a result, an employee received an excess transfer of IDR 5,000,000 last month.When you confirmed today, the employee argued that the money had been used to pay personal debts.

pertanyaan.1: In terms of employment regulations and empathy, why are you prohibited from deducting IDR 5,000,000 in full from your salary next month, and who are the 2 internal parties you are obliged to report first regarding this carelessness?
pertanyaan.2: Write 1 sentence of a tactical offer to the employee to find a middle way to return the money without making his salary next month completely empty/minus!
pertanyaan.3: Design a manual approval flow (Approval Workflow) before the salary transfer file is sent to the bank, so that unreasonable amounts can be detected by other parties!

2.judul: Case Study 2 — Overtime Claim Manipulation (Funds Leakage)
2.deskripsi: The Warehouse division's overtime bill tripled.The overtime form has indeed been approved by the Warehouse Manager, but physically it doesn't make sense (some staff claim 60 hours of overtime/week).The warehouse manager is angry and tells you to just pay straight away because he already has his signature.

pertanyaan.1: Apart from looking at the paper overtime form, mention 2 pieces of real data evidence from other departments that you would pull to prove that this overtime is fictitious!
pertanyaan.2: Write 1 counter argument to the Warehouse Manager linking this overtime irregularity to potential financial losses and a company financial audit!
pertanyaan.3: If the evidence of manipulation is strong, decide whether the overtime bill will be withheld or still disbursed, then create a rule for capping overtime hours so that the company budget doesn't break out of control!

3.judul: Case Study 3 — Tax Dilemma (Angry Employees Take Home Pay Down)
3.deskripsi: Because the government's tax regulations have changed, this month's PPh 21 deduction is bigger.A senior employee comes to your desk angrily, accusing the Payroll team of secretly deducting his salary, and threatening to resign if his taxes are not covered by the company (Gross-up).

pertanyaan.1: Why is responding to the employee's anger by telling him to "Read the tax rules yourself on Google" a fatal communication error for an HR person?
pertanyaan.2: Write a short explanation (maximum 3 sentences) in layman's language confirming that the deduction money was purely deposited into the State treasury, accompanied by 1 physical document that you will show him on the table!
pertanyaan.3: Propose 1 proactive step from the Payroll division next month so that mass panic about tax deductions can be prevented before pay slips are distributed!

4.judul: Case Study 4 — Salary Dispute for Sudden Resignation of Employees
4.deskripsi: An employee resigned today without saying goodbye (even though the resignation rule is One Month Notice / 30 days in advance).He demanded that his salary for the last 15 working days be immediately transferred today and was afraid he would report it to the police/Manpower Department because the company was deemed to be "withholding his salary rights."

pertanyaan.1: As a Payroll, what is your strongest argument for daring to withhold your salary temporarily, and what 2 obligations/facilities must be ensured to be completed before the salary is released?
pertanyaan.2: Write a short draft message (WhatsApp/Email) that firmly refuses to transfer his salary today, but includes absolute conditions that he must fulfill if he wants the money to be disbursed!
pertanyaan.3: So that this case of an employee suddenly leaving doesn't cause any more trouble for the company, what special warning clause (penalty) must be added to the Employment Agreement sheet for new employees in the future?

5.judul: Case Study 5 — Crisis Management (Bank System/Payroll Down on the D Day)
5.deskripsi: Today is the 25th (Payday) at 14.00 noon.Suddenly, the central Internet Banking system experienced an error and could not be accessed for an unspecified time.Hundreds of employees were anxious and started spreading rumors that the company was bankrupt.

pertanyaan.1: Your first action is to stop wild gossip.Write a 1 sentence official announcement (Broadcast) that is honest, reassuring, without promising a specific time when the banking system will return to normal.
pertanyaan.2: If the bank only recovers the next day and an employee is fined for late mortgage payments due to a late salary, is the company obliged to reimburse the employee for the bank fine?Give reasons.
pertanyaan.3: Develop an Emergency Plan (Contingency Plan) with the Finance team to disburse salaries on the same day, especially for lower level employees (such as Office Boy and Security) whose money has been used up for food.

1.judul: Case 1 — Setting User Expectations (Unreasonable Criteria)
1.deskripsi:
The IT Manager (User) asks you to look for a Programmer with 8 years of experience and mastery of 5 difficult programming languages, but the salary budget is only equivalent to junior staff.
• A month passes, no candidates have applied.
• Users are angry and accuse the HRD department of slow work.

pertanyaan.1: Write 1 assertive sentence along with evidence of real data (market conditions) that you will convey to users to break the accusation of "slow HRD" and at the same time make them aware that their criteria are unreasonable.
pertanyaan.2: If the absolute salary budget cannot be increased, which option will you encourage Users to approve: Lowering experience requirements OR Providing non-financial benefits?Give 1 tactical reason.
pertanyaan.3: Design 1 mandatory rule (SOP / Service Level Agreement) that must be agreed upon between HRD and Users before any vacancy is published, so that this incident does not happen again.

2.judul: Case 2 — Champion Candidate Affected by Counter-Offer
2.deskripsi:
You found your dream candidate.He has signed the Offering Letter and is scheduled to enter on Monday.
• Suddenly on Friday, he withdrew because he was detained by his old company.
• Candidates are offered salary increases and surprise promotions at their old places.

pertanyaan.1: Should our company also increase the salary offer?If not, write 1 psychological question on the phone to sway his decision to stay in the old place.
pertanyaan.2: If he still doesn't join, write a draft of a tactical sentence to call and offer him the 2nd Place (Runner Up) candidate, even though last week you already sent him a rejection email!
pertanyaan.3: What "Commitment Locking" tactics should you implement in the final stages of the Interview (before the salary offer) so that the risk of the candidate receiving a counter-offer from their old company can be prevented?

3.judul: Case 3 — Mass Ghosting Case (Empty First Day of Work)
3.deskripsi:
There are 3 Customer Service (CS) candidates who have passed the selection and agreed to enter the office at 8 this morning.
• At 9 am, not a single candidate showed up at the office.
• Calls are not picked up, and when WhatsApp is only read (ghosting).
• Users really need additional people today.

pertanyaan.1: What is the most rational and non-defensive explanation that you would give to the User (CS Manager) that day regarding the 3 people who ran away?
pertanyaan.2: The time lag between signing the contract and the first day of work is often an opportunity for candidates to run away/change their minds.Plan 1 simple Pre-Boarding activity during that break to bond them emotionally!
pertanyaan.3: For positions with a high turnover rate such as CS, mention 1 strategy for building a "Talent Pool (Reserve)" system so that you can immediately call a replacement person within 1x24 hours!

4.judul: Case 4 — Reference Check Dilemma (Dark Past)
4.deskripsi:
You have a smart Financial Supervisor candidate and Users really like him.
• When you secretly call HR at his old company (Reference Check), you get a tip that this candidate used to embezzle office cash.
• The case was finally covered up by the old company internally.

pertanyaan.1: Don't immediately believe in 1 source.Apart from looking for references from other parties, write 1 trick question (Behavioral Question) during the follow-up interview to provoke the candidate's honesty about the difference in money.
pertanyaan.2: If the user snarks and says: "Just accept it! He's smart, just leave his past alone," write down 1 rebuttal argument from HRD that focuses on fatal risks in the future!
pertanyaan.3: If the President Director finally insists that the candidate is still accepted, what legal protective documents/administrative requirements must HRD add to the Employment Agreement in order to protect the company?

5.judul: Case 5 — Candidate Internal vs. External Conflict
5.deskripsi:
There is a vacancy for Branch Head.You have internal candidates (old employees, loyal for 5 years, but less aggressive).
• On the other hand, there are External candidates (outsiders, very aggressive, ambitious, but ask for high salaries).
• Users want to recruit outsiders, while the internal team starts to argue that their career path is not valued.

pertanyaan.1: What real data (aside from absence and length of work) do you have to pull to objectively prove to the User whether the Internal Candidate is worthy of consideration or not?
pertanyaan.2: If in the end an External Candidate (outsider) is recruited, how do HRD and Users convey the news of the rejection to the Internal Candidate without destroying their work motivation and then resigning?
pertanyaan.3: If the outsider is still recruited but the salary request exceeds the standard (budget) of the Branch Head, what are your tactics for managing the salary components (for example: Basic Salary vs Incentive/Bonus ratio) so that the company's total fixed cost burden does not fall?

1.judul: Case Study 1 — Machine Schedule Push-Pull (Focus: PPIC Scheduling & Coordination)
1.deskripsi:
You have scheduled Preventive Maintenance (PM) for the Main Machine on Wednesday for 6 hours.
• On Tuesday afternoon, the PPIC team refused to turn off the machine because there was an urgent order that had to be sent on Thursday.
• The mechanic warns you: "If you don't service the machine tomorrow, the next day the machine will definitely break down completely."

pertanyaan.1: As a Job Planner who is in the middle, what data or technical facts must you show to PPIC so that they realize that delaying maintenance will actually destroy their own targets?
pertanyaan.2: Design a middle ground scheme (schedule compromise) between the mechanic and PPIC so that urgent orders are still completed, but the machine still gets maintenance within a safe time limit.
pertanyaan.3: Create a written agreement (SLA) between the Maintenance department and PPIC regarding the maximum limit for PM schedule delays, so that the schedule you create is not always sacrificed.

2.judul: Case 2 — Spare Parts Emergency & Central Delay (Focus: Procurement & Logistics)
2.deskripsi:
The engine repair schedule is scheduled for Friday.You have made a Purchase Request (PR) since last week to the Purchasing team in Surabaya.
• This Thursday the goods have not arrived.
• When called, Purchasing Surabaya answered: "The vendor is still looking for the goods, just wait."
• If the goods do not arrive tomorrow, the repair is canceled and the mechanic is unemployed.

pertanyaan.1: What technical contingency steps will you take with local vendors to save the allocated mechanical work schedule?
pertanyaan.2: If the goods finally arrive on Friday but the quantity is lacking (order 5, arrive 3), what will be the fatal impact on the Inventory Valuation data, Safety Stock calculations, and Reorder Point (ROP) automation in the system if you are forced to input a full Good Receipt Note (GRN)?
pertanyaan.3: Based on this case of delay, how do you recalculate the Lead Time for procurement of these components to update the Max-Min Stock parameters in the warehouse so that a similar breakdown does not happen again in the future?

3.judul: Case 3 — End of Month Cut-Off Disaster (Focus: Dual System Management - Excel vs Accurate)
3.deskripsi:
Today is the monthly Cut-Off (book closing) schedule.You have to adjust the data.
• In your Excel manual notes, the remaining lubricating oil is 5 drums.
• However, when checked with the Accurate system, stock was recorded as only having 3 drums left.
• There is a difference of 2 drums lost between systems.

pertanyaan.1: From the Audit Trail system side, mention 2 administrative gaps that most often cause stock variances for consumables (such as oil/grease) between the Accurate system and Excel records in the field.
pertanyaan.2: What physical tracking actions and short-term document investigations should you undertake that very day before making a decision to adjust the numbers in the system?
pertanyaan.3: If after a physical check it turns out that the remaining oil is indeed 3 drums (your Excel notes were wrong), what technical supporting documents must you attach to the Finance department so that the difference between the 2 drums is approved as an operational cost, not a loss due to negligence.

4.judul: Case 4 — Machine Parts Cannibals (Focus: Asset Management & PR Administration)
4.deskripsi:
Machine B suddenly became seriously damaged (Breakdown).Mechanics need engine sensors ASAP.
• Because the stock in the warehouse was empty, the Chief Mechanic decided to remove the sensor from Machine C which was idle.
• The sensor is installed on Machine B so that factory activities continue.

pertanyaan.1: To tidy up the administration after this cannibalistic incident, how do you create a new Purchase Request (PR): Do you order sensors for "Engine B repair" or "Replace Engine C sensor"?Give reasons.
pertanyaan.2: Design an emergency intervention protocol or SOP that mechanics must fulfill before carrying out cannibalization, so that the history of machine damage and the structure of the Bill of Materials (BOM) for both machines in the Accurate system can still be tracked accurately.
pertanyaan.3: What are the long-term risks to the depreciation value and reliability of Machine C if this covert cannibalization practice continues unchecked by a Job Planner?

5.judul: Case 5 — Supervision Gap After 11pm (Focus: Stock Control & Handover)
5.deskripsi:
Your working hours as a Job Planner are only until 11 pm.You leave the key to the spare parts cupboard with the Chief Mechanic (Supervisor) so that his team can still retrieve the goods if the machine breaks down at night.
• Three times you have found that the stock of goods in the morning is reduced, but no mechanic has reported it in the WhatsApp group.
• When asked, the Chief Mechanic reasoned: "Wow, I went around the factory last night, I don't know which subordinate opened the cupboard and took the goods."

pertanyaan.1: As an inventory authorization owner, why is this "key lock" system without strict regulations dangerous for your position during stock taking audits by Finance?How do you map out legal responsibility for these material differences?
pertanyaan.2: Create a mechanism for handing over warehouse keys and strict stock verification at 23.00 before you go home, so that the night shift supervisor takes full responsibility for the movement of goods.
pertanyaan.3: How do you design a physical layout scheme for an emergency warehouse (Night Shift Kitting Buffer) to separate critical components that can be picked up independently by night mechanics, without having to provide full access to the main locked warehouse area?

1.judul: Case Study 1 — Petty Cash Calculation Differences and Closed Book Issues
1.deskripsi:
You manage petty cash using the fixed balance method (funds are set at IDR 10,000,000).On October 31, when the October books are locked (closed), you count the contents of the safe and find the following data:
Components in the SafeNominalDescription
Physical CashIDR 2,000,000Payments of banknotes & coins
Bon/Expenditure NoteRp 7,000,000Dated 25 - 30 October
Cashbon Bond (IOU)Rp 500,000Employee A (No note yet)

Total Physical & Documents: Rp. 9,500,000 (There is a difference of less than Rp. 500,000)

pertanyaan.1: In your opinion, what is the most logical operational reason why the money in the safe could be less than IDR 500,000?As a cash holder, what is the first action you will take to track it?
pertanyaan.2: Because the October bookkeeping has already been locked while the Rp. 7,000,000 note has not yet been input into the computer, what bad effect will this have on the accuracy of the company's profit and loss report in October?
pertanyaan.3: In November, you must refill petty cash so that the balance returns to IDR 10,000,000.How do you input the October notes into the system in November so that your bookkeeping remains neat and correct?

2.judul: Case Study 2 — Examination of Expenditure Evidence and Indications of Fraud
2.deskripsi:
List of applications for Petty Cash reimbursement from the Marketing Division this week:
DateExpenditure DescriptionNominalSupporting Evidence
Saturday, Nov 14Client Entertainment (Dinner)Rp 1,900,000EDC Receipt (Without menu details)
Monday, Nov 16Purchase Printer Ink (Shop A)Rp 900,000Handwritten Note
Monday, Nov 16HVS Paper Purchase (Shop A)Rp 800,000Handwritten Note

(SOP Note: Maximum limit for 1x petty cash transaction is IDR 1,000,000)

pertanyaan.1: Based on the data above, find 2 irregularities or frauds that violate the company's maximum transaction limit rules.
pertanyaan.2: Why is a purchase at Store A on November 16 considered circumventing the rules?What are the bad risks for you as a cashier if you pass the transaction?
pertanyaan.3: Before you approve the November 14 dinner claim, what additional supporting evidence are you required to request from the employee to prove it was for office business, not personal?

3.judul: Case Study 3 — Petty Cash Foreign Currencies (Dollars) and Exchange Differences
3.deskripsi:
You manage petty cash using US Dollars with a fixed balance of $500.Mutation records during December:
DateActivityPhysical USDSystem Rate (BI)
Dec 1Month Beginning Balance$ 500Rp 15,000 / USD
Dec 15Pay Taxi for Foreign Guests($ 100)Rp 15,300 / USD
Dec 31Final Balance (Not yet filled in)$ 400Rp 15,500 / USD

pertanyaan.1: When you input a $100 taxi expense on December 15, why does the computer system require you to enter that day's rate (Rp. 15,300) and not the rate at the beginning of the month (Rp. 15,000)?

1.judul: Case Study 1 – Stock Opname Difference
1.deskripsi:
During the monthly stock taking, quite large stock differences were found in several materials.
• It is known that there are still transactions that have not been input into the system.
• Some materials were taken by the production department without official documents.
• The stock checking process is not carried out routinely, so system data is different from physical data and interferes with purchasing and production planning.

pertanyaan.1: What is your first emergency action to 'secure' the data system so that more serious order or production errors do not occur during the investigation process?
pertanyaan.2: How do you actually prove that this difference is purely due to 'admin negligence' or 'bad production habits of taking goods without permission' so that you don't take the wrong action?
pertanyaan.3: What concrete procedures will you create so that the collection of goods must be recorded in the system immediately, and how will you force the production department to follow these rules?

2.judul: Case Study 2 – Stock Data Mismatch and Production Stops
2.deskripsi:
The production process stopped because the main material ran out, even though the ERP system still showed available stock (on-hand).When checked, the warehouse was empty.
• Initial investigations found two main gaps: the existence of rejected goods that had not been processed out of the system.
• Frequent collection of materials for sudden needs that staff did not have time to input into the ERP system.
• Management demands in-depth evaluation so that data integrity between system and physics is back in sync.

pertanyaan.1: How do you carry out an audit to dissect whether this non-conformity is caused by human error (delay in administrative input) or workflow failure (issue of goods without official documents), so that you can determine appropriate corrective steps?
pertanyaan.2: When management demands stock certainty in the midst of chaos, what are the first tactical steps you take to provide accurate updated data to the Production and Purchasing teams without having to completely stop warehouse operations to carry out a complete stock take?
pertanyaan.3: How do you design a system for separating goods status in ERP so that the system no longer displays goods that have been damaged or ordered as ready stock, to ensure that ERP data always reflects real physical conditions in real-time?

3.judul: Case Study 3 – Warehouse Performance Declines
3.deskripsi:
In the last three months, warehouse performance has fallen.Searching for goods takes a long time, delivery is often late, and picking up the wrong goods is becoming more common.
• The condition is made worse by the large number of new staff who do not understand their duties.
• The workload is increasing, resulting in continuous overtime.
• The director asks you to improve your work methods so that the warehouse becomes effective again.

pertanyaan.1: How can you use error tracking data to objectively prove whether the main problem is warehouse layout, staff competency gaps, or workflow inefficiencies?
pertanyaan.2: What concrete steps can you implement within 30 days to re-layout or improve SOPs so that the warehouse is more agile without requiring additional budget?
pertanyaan.3: What KPIs do you set to measure operational effectiveness so the Director can see the correlation between system improvements and reduced overtime costs?

4.judul: Case Study 4 – Alleged Loss of Material
4.deskripsi:
During the last six months the company experienced material losses of quite large value.
• Audit results showed that some materials left the warehouse based only on verbal instructions.
• Vehicle inspections are not carried out consistently and supervision in the warehouse area is still weak.
• The Board of Directors asked the Warehouse Head to conduct an investigation and develop a better control system.

pertanyaan.1: How do you verify audit results between system expenditure records and physical data to map loss patterns (what time, what material, who is on duty) without damaging team morale?
pertanyaan.2: Between verbal instructions, weak exit controls, or incomplete documentation, which do you think is the main triggering factor and why is this control an absolute priority to improve?
pertanyaan.3: How do you design a Double-Check flow or separation of duties in the first 30 days so that every gram of outgoing goods must have a physical/digital footprint that cannot be interfered with personally?

5.judul: Case Study 5 – Conflict between Warehouse and Production
5.deskripsi:
The relationship between the warehouse and production began to deteriorate because there were frequent delays in material delivery.
• The production team assesses that the warehouse is working too slowly.
• The warehouse team reasoned that material requests were often sudden, picking documents were incomplete, and the number of available workers was limited.
• This condition affects production targets and gives rise to mutual blaming.

pertanyaan.1: How do you use records (data) of delays and the number of sudden requests to make both teams aware that the problem is in the work system, not because of mutual hatred or blaming between people?
pertanyaan.2: How do you create fair rules: on the one hand, production can guarantee delivery on time, but on the other hand, the warehouse is not overwhelmed by sudden and continuous demand?
pertanyaan.3: How do you make a rule that goods cannot go out without official documents, but still have a way out if there is a truly emergency or urgent situation?

1.deskripsi:

2.judul: Case Study 2 — Delay in Delivery of Goods
2.deskripsi:
The company received complaints from customers because the delivery of raw materials was late for 5 days.As a result, the customer's production process stopped temporarily.

Investigation results:
  • The goods were packed on time.
  • The new truck was available two days later.
  • The shipping documents were only completed the day after the truck arrived.
  • There was a queue for loading and unloading at the central warehouse.

pertanyaan.1: Based on this case, in which process does the biggest bottleneck occur?Explain your reasons.
pertanyaan.2: If you were a Logistics Supervisor, what short-term and long-term corrective actions would be taken?
pertanyaan.3: What KPIs need to be monitored so that delivery delays can be minimized?

3.judul: Case Study 3 — Overstock and Slow Moving Inventory
3.deskripsi:
At the end of the quarter the following conditions were found:
  • Inventory value increased 35%.
  • Customer demand fell 20%.
  • Warehouse capacity has been filled 95%.
  • Many items have not moved for more than 180 days.

pertanyaan.1: What operational and financial risks can arise due to overstock and slow moving inventory conditions?
pertanyaan.2: What steps will you take to reduce slow moving inventory without disrupting the company's operational needs?
pertanyaan.3: What data needs to be analyzed before the company decides to purchase the next item?

1.judul: Case 1: Finding of Tax Withholding Errors During One Tax Year
1.deskripsi:
In the internal audit process, it was discovered that the company made errors withholding and collecting tax on several transactions during one tax year.
• Service transactions that should be subject to Income Tax Article 23 are not deducted.
• There are transactions that are deducted at the wrong rate and some are subject to the wrong type of tax.
• As a result, there are differences between transactions in financial reports, withholding receipts, and company tax reporting.
• Errors were not identified in the previous period's audit, thereby potentially giving rise to corrections and sanctions during inspection by the DGT.

pertanyaan.1: Analyze the possible causes of tax withholding errors during one year.In your opinion, is this problem caused more by a weak understanding of taxation, weaknesses in internal control, or non-compliance with company procedures?Explain your reasons.
pertanyaan.2: If you are accepted as the PIC Audit Team, what audit procedures will you carry out to identify all transactions that experience tax withholding errors and ensure the company's compliance with tax provisions?
pertanyaan.3: If the audit results show that tax withholding errors have persisted for a full year, what recommendations would you convey to management regarding corrective steps, risk mitigation, and improving internal controls so that similar errors do not happen again?

2.judul: Case 2: Evaluation of SPI Accounting & Limited Audit Time
2.deskripsi:
The company has 5 Regional Offices which manage the Accounting process with total transactions of IDR 100 billion.The materiality limit set by the Audit Committee is IDR 2 billion.
• The Internal Audit Team consists of 3 auditors and only has 3 working days to evaluate the effectiveness of SPI Accounting.
• In testing in Regional A, it was found that 8% of the transactions tested had control weaknesses (no approval, late reconciliation, and journals without supporting documents).

pertanyaan.1: If a level of control weakness of 8% is assumed to occur throughout the region, calculate the estimated value of the affected transactions and analyze whether the potential risk exceeds the materiality threshold of IDR 2 billion.
pertanyaan.2: With only 2 days remaining for the audit, what sampling method would you choose to evaluate SPI Accounting?Explain the reasons and implementation strategy.
pertanyaan.3: If the estimation results indicate a material risk but management rejects the results because the audit was carried out using sampling techniques and limited time, how will you prepare the audit report and what steps will you take to maintain objectivity, accountability and legal protection for the audit team?

3.judul: Case 3: Negligence of the Audit Team during Stock Taking at the Client PT
3.deskripsi:
You bring the audit team to the Client PT for Stock Opname (SO) and Accurate system reconciliation.Once done, the data is a mess due to your junior team's negligence:
• They forget to ensure that warehouse operations are frozen, so that goods still go in and out when they are counted.
• They entered the wrong unit of goods (Pcs vs Box) in Accurate.
• Meanwhile, tomorrow morning is the Closing Meeting schedule with the Client's Directors.

pertanyaan.1: How does your team's negligence undermine the reliability of the entire audit report?How do you assess whether this messy data can still be corrected or is it completely invalid?
pertanyaan.2: Considering the Closing Meeting is scheduled for tomorrow morning, what tactical decisions do you take?Do you recalculate, do back-tracing, or postpone the meeting?Explain the risks!
pertanyaan.3: How do you explain your team's procedural errors to the Client's Directors professionally without blaming your subordinates?What control steps will you implement on your team in the future so that this fatal mistake does not happen again?

4.judul: Case 4: Difference in Goods Recording Date between Cortax and Accurate
4.deskripsi:
It was found that there was a difference in the date of receipt of goods between the Coretax and Accurate systems.In Accurate, goods are recorded as being received in one tax period, whereas in Coretax new transactions are recorded in the next tax period.
• This causes Input VAT to be credited in the wrong tax period (a discrepancy arises in tax data vs financial statements).
• This condition has occurred since the previous quarterly audit, but the audit team at that time did not reconcile data, did not check supporting documents, and did not review the system change log, thereby potentially leading to tax audit corrections.

pertanyaan.1: Based on the case above, analyze the most likely cause of the difference in recording dates between Coretax and Accurate.In your opinion, are these problems caused more by system weaknesses, operational procedure errors, or weak internal controls?Explain your reasons.
pertanyaan.2: If you are accepted as the PIC Audit Team, what audit procedures will you implement to ensure data compatibility between Coretax and Accurate so that differences in recording dates can be detected early?
pertanyaan.3: If this finding is only discovered after the company has finished reporting the Periodic VAT SPT, how will you assess the level of audit risk, its impact on the company, and the priority actions that must be taken immediately by management?Explain your reasons.

5.judul: Case 5: Aspects of Audit Team Negligence (Audit Adjusting Journal Error)
5.deskripsi:
In the process of finalizing PTSenior Audit instructs Junior Audit to draft an Audit Adjustment Journal.
• Because he was tired of chasing deadlines, Audit Junior compiled the journal logic incorrectly:
    (Debit) Salaries & Wages Expense: IDR 2.5 Billion
    (Credit) Cash and Cash Equivalents: IDR 2.5 Billion
• This draft is immediately included in the main Audit Working Paper (KKP) without being reviewed by Senior Audit, and is immediately submitted to client management.

pertanyaan.1: Based on accrual-based accounting standards, analyze why the journal draft made by the audit team is wrong in principle.Show what impact (domino effect) the error in crediting the Cash account had on the company's Cash Flow Statement and Balance Sheet (Statement of Financial Position) in the current year.
pertanyaan.2: Why can a junior's mistake slip through to the final draft report?Explain the concept of multilevel review in audit standards that was violated by the Audit Team and what your recommendations are so that KAP (Public Accounting Firm) does not repeat similar negligence.
pertanyaan.3: If the company management (client) was the first to discover the audit team's mistake, what would be the impact on the KAP's reputation?What professional actions should the Audit Partner take to defuse this situation without losing credibility?

1.judul: Case Study 1 — 30 Minute Time Range Output (Circumference/Filter Length Deviates)
1.deskripsi:
You carry out routine checks on Machine A. At 10.00, the results of measuring the circumference and length of the filter are very good (normal).
• However, when the check was scheduled at 10.30, the filter size suddenly became smaller and had Out of Spec (OOS/Reject) status.
• The machine operator said: "Just throw away the 10.30 filter, the 10.00 to 10.29 filter is definitely still a good size."

pertanyaan.1: Why, according to Quality Control regulations, are you strictly prohibited from believing the operator's statement that "production from 10.00 to 10.29 must be good"?
pertanyaan.2: What absolute decision must you make regarding all cigarette filters produced in baskets/cardboards from 10.00 to 10.30?
pertanyaan.3: To determine exactly when the machine started producing the wrong size, what kind of search (investigation) actions would you perform on the stack of filters in that bucket?

2.judul: Case 2 — Discovery of Critical Visual Defect (Exposed Paper Glue)
2.deskripsi:
When taking 20 routine filter samples per 30 minutes, you find 2 rods that have an Open Seam defect (the glue on the paper wrapping the filter is open/not sticking).
• The machine operator gets angry when you ask for the machine to be turned off.
• He reasoned: "That's only 2 broken rods out of thousands of filters that come out per minute! Just keep running the machine!"

pertanyaan.1: Why is finding “only 2 sticks” of filters with exposed glue in a small sample (20 sticks) a big red flag for the overall production of that watch?
pertanyaan.2: Write 1 firm but professional sentence to force the operator to turn off the machine so that he repairs the glue line first.
pertanyaan.3: Apart from holding production for the last 30 minutes, what specific instructions will you give the Sort (manual inspection) team to handle the problematic filter cartons?

3.judul: Case 3 — Pressure Drop Fluctuations (Unstable Suction Power)
3.deskripsi:
During the 30 minute check, you test the Pressure Drop (PD/filter density) using a measuring instrument.
• The results are very unstable: there are 5 very dense filters, 5 very light filters, and the rest are normal.
• Usually the test results are always uniform.

pertanyaan.1: If the results in just one sample pull are very unstable (fluctuating), what 2 possible technical problems are occurring with the raw material (tow) or the running of the production machine?
pertanyaan.2: Why would a filter with a Pressure Drop that goes up and down (not uniform) be so detrimental to cigarette consumers when they smoke it?
pertanyaan.3: What specific data (from your test results) are you required to show to the Mechanic/Mechanical Technician so that they believe that the machine is unstable and needs immediate repair?

4.judul: Case 4 — Late Check Incident (Missed Machine Sampling)
4.deskripsi:
Because you were busy handling the rejected filter on Machine A, you were late for the sample collection schedule on Machine B.
• You just took a sample from Machine B at the 60th minute (1 cycle missed).
• Sample test results at the 60th minute showed a soft filter (lacking hardener/Triacetin).

pertanyaan.1: What is the most fatal loss/risk for the factory due to your 30 minute delay in checking Machine B?
pertanyaan.2: Because the status was "conceded" for 1 hour without checking, what status (Release, Hold, or Reject) would you immediately give to all filter boxes from Machine B for the last 1 hour?Give reasons.
pertanyaan.3: Design a time management/communication procedure if you are alone looking after several machines, so that the schedule for taking samples every 30 minutes is no longer missed even if you are busy on one machine.

5.judul: Case 5 — Dust vs Black Flaw Conflict (Dirt on Filter)
5.deskripsi:
During a routine 30 minute visual inspection, you notice black spots/spots on the white part of the filter rod.
• The machine operator rubbed it with his hands and said: "This is just ordinary machine dust, rub it and it will disappear. Is it time to reject it?"
• Visually the stain looks like a dry oil spot.

pertanyaan.1: As a QC Analyst, why are you prohibited from tolerating dirty filters even though the dirt "can be removed if scrubbed"?
pertanyaan.2: To prove to the operator that it is an oil spot defect, what simple physical test method do you perform on the filter in front of his eyes?
pertanyaan.3: The machine had to be cleaned, but the operator refused because he was pursuing production targets.What is the reporting escalation flow (who is the boss you call) to execute a machine stop at that very minute?

1.judul: Case Study 1 — Price Wars and Payment Terms (Focus: Presentations & Offers)
1.deskripsi:
You are presenting at a medium-scale cigarette factory.The owner is interested in ordering filters in large quantities.
• But he asks for a "crazy" discounted price that is close to your factory capital.
• The client also requested a relaxation of payment terms to 60 days credit (usually a maximum of 30 days).

pertanyaan.1: What is the biggest financial risk for our factory if you as a Salesperson just accept a large volume order from a new client with a 60 day credit payment term?
pertanyaan.2: Arrange a counter-offer tactic so that you can still get that large order, but the payment terms are much safer for our company's cash.
pertanyaan.3: When is the right time for a Sales person to have the courage to say "No" (walk away) and let go of that big prospective client?Give 1 objective reason.

2.judul: Case 2 — Sample Generation Time Conflict (Focus: Overseeing the Sampling & R&D Process)
2.deskripsi:
The client tested your filter sample and found it not quite right (the suction power was too dense).
• The client asks you to bring a new lighter sample within 3 days.
• Internally at the factory, the R&D/Production team said the trial machine schedule was full and new samples could be completed in 7 days at the earliest.

pertanyaan.1: Why is the Sales habit of always agreeing to client requests ("Ready, 3 days, sir!") before checking the capacity of the internal R&D team a fatal mistake?
pertanyaan.2: If a client threatens to move competitors because they don't want to wait 7 days, what technical compromise strategy can you offer to the internal R&D team or the client?
pertanyaan.3: Design a communication flow agreement (SLA) between the Sales team and the R&D team so that in the future sample production schedule conflicts like this can be anticipated early.

3.judul: Case 3 — Delivery Promise vs Factory Capacity (Focus: Order Management & PPIC)
3.deskripsi:
At the end of the month, you get an impromptu Purchase Order (PO) from a VIP client.
• To make the client happy, you immediately promise that the goods will be sent on Friday this week.
• PPIC rejected the order because the machine was producing another client's queue.
• The VIP client's goods can only be finished on Tuesday next week.

pertanyaan.1: If you force PPIC to squeeze in this VIP client's order and sacrifice other clients' schedules, what domino effect will occur in the Good Finish Warehouse and the factory as a whole?
pertanyaan.2: Since the error in the promise lies with you, what kind of Partial Delivery strategy will you propose to PPIC and the VIP client?How do you calculate minimum running stock?
pertanyaan.3: Before receiving a physical PO sheet/PDF from a client, what 2 operational things should a Salesperson always ask the PPIC and Warehouse team?

4.judul: Case 4 — Facing an Angry Client Due to Defects (Focus: Complaint Handling & QC)
4.deskripsi:
A VIP client calls you furious.Their cigarette machines often jam because a lot of the glue on your factory-made filters comes off (open seam).
• The client claims that 20 boxes were damaged and demands 100% money back immediately.
• The factory's QC team investigated and found that only 2 boxes were defective, while the other 18 boxes were purely an error in the client's own cigarette machine settings.

pertanyaan.1: When a client is angry on the phone, why is it strictly forbidden for a Salesperson to immediately say the words: "Okay sir, we admit we were wrong and we will immediately compensate you"?
pertanyaan.2: The client insisted your factory was 100% at fault.Explain how you would communicate the QC findings (that only 2 boxes were damaged) to clients, without offending their feelings or making them feel accused of lying.
pertanyaan.3: If it is finally agreed that the goods will be returned, why does Sales have to ensure that the physical filters withdrawn from the client's factory are actually your factory's Batch number (production code)?

5.judul: Case 5 — Personal Goals vs Long Term Relationships (Focus: Keeping Clients & Pursuing Goals)
5.deskripsi:
It's the 28th day (end of the month), and you're still 15% short of reaching your monthly sales target.
• There is one cigarette factory that you are very loyal to, but the stock of filters in their warehouse is actually still enough for the next month.
• If they want to order now, your target will definitely be achieved.

pertanyaan.1: What are the long-term risks to the business relationship (trust) if you “force” or beg these loyal clients to buy things they don't need yet, just for your personal goals?
pertanyaan.2: Design a tactical offer that is mutually beneficial (win-win solution), so that the client is tempted to issue a PO today even though the goods will only be sent/used next month.
pertanyaan.3: If the client still refuses to order this month and your target ultimately fails to be achieved, what kind of data/defense report will you present to your Sales Manager?

1.judul: Case Study 1 — Active Stores Start Dropping Orders
1.deskripsi:
You handle the building materials distribution area with an active store network.In the last 2 months, 6 major stores in your area started reducing purchases.They're still buying, but the volume is down quite significantly.After evaluation, several causes were found:

  • Competitors' prices are cheaper.

If this condition is left unchecked, it will be difficult to achieve monthly sales targets and the coverage area may weaken.

pertanyaan.1: How do you analyze the causes of the decline in orders from these stores?
pertanyaan.2: What steps will you take in the first week to restore sales in that area?
pertanyaan.3: If company discounts are limited, how do you still encourage increased orders from customers?

2.judul: Case Study 2 — Distributor Requests Longer Terms and Additional Programs
2.deskripsi:

pertanyaan.1: How do you assess whether the distributor's request is still business-sound or is it too risky for the company?
pertanyaan.2: How do you put together a proposal that remains attractive to distributors but still maintains company profits?
